scene.bubble: Read about presentation day, learn to join your ideas with connectors, then share your own year.
scene.intro: This is the last unit of the year, and it is presentation day for the Inspiring Nordic project. In this unit you read Mateo's blog about the big day, you learn how to join your ideas with connectors — and, but, because and so — and you prepare your own short presentation. You have learned so much this year. Now it's time to be proud and share it. The stage is yours!

data.author: mateo
data.title: Presentation day!
data.text:
Today was presentation day for our Inspiring Nordic project, and it was the best day of the year!

Each group had three minutes to share its work. My group talked about local jobs in our town, because we think they are important. We were a little nervous, but we practised a lot, so in the end we spoke clearly.

Nadia showed our poster, and everyone loved her drawings. Sofía read a short poem at the end, and the whole class listened quietly. Liam gave his opinion with a good reason: “I like this project because we learn about real life, not just books.”

When we finished, the audience clapped. Our teacher was very proud of us, and so were we. I have learned so much this year: I can read, write, listen, speak — and work in a team.

What about you? What are you most proud of this year? Tell us and share your best moment!

data.title: Connectors: and, but, because, so
data.intro: Connectors join ideas and make your speaking and writing flow. Each one has a different job.
rules: and adds an idea; but shows a difference or a surprise.
because gives a reason (why); so gives a result (what happened next).
Use a comma before but and so in a long sentence.

items.sentence: I like our project ___ it is about real jobs.
Mateo is shy, ___ he spoke very clearly.
We finished the poster, ___ we started the poem.
The talk was short ___ very interesting.

activities.title: Exam task · Reading & Writing — read the poem, then choose the answer.

data.text:
My Nordic Year
This year I learned to read and write,
to share my work and get it right.
I built, I spoke, I read a book,
I helped my friends, I gave, I took.
And now I stand up, proud and tall —
I am not shy at all!

activities.title: Speaking — give a mini-presentation. In pairs, then record it.

data.text: Give a one-minute mini-presentation about your Inspiring Nordic year, like a TED talk. Model: “This year I am proud of my project, because I learned to work in a team.” Say: one thing you have learned, one thing you are proud of, and your opinion about the project (with a reason using because). Look at your audience and speak clearly. Then record your presentation.

homework.prompt: Write a short paragraph (6–8 sentences) about your Inspiring Nordic year to read on presentation day. Say what you have learned, what you are proud of, and your opinion of the project — join your ideas with because, and, but and so. Capital letters and full stops!
